To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the extent to Which women perceive men's voices to possess physical dominance and low (i.e. trustworthiness) is associated with the magnitude of the difference in their preferences for masculine men in long-term and short- term relationships.

women's preferences for low-pitched voices in men are associated with their perceptions that these men have high levels of physical dominance and are not trustworthy, and that these associations are stronger for women who prefer low-pitched men as short-term rather than as long-term mates.
the effect of relationship type on women's preferences is moderated by their perceptions of men's physical dominance and trust.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that individual differences in personality play in shaping variation in the effect of the relationship context on women’s preferences for men with masculine voices.
the question of why women sometimes prefer men with masculine voices and sometimes prefer men with feminine voices.
how women's preferences for men's voices are influenced by the context of the relationship, and how individual differences in women may affect these preferences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the variation of the extent to which individuals attribute negative personality characteristics predicts individual differences in preferences for masculine men.
Variation in the extent to Which Women Attribute Physical Dominance and Low Trustworthiness to Masculine Men's Voices Predicts Individual Differences in Women's Masculinity Preferences.

The extent to which women prefer masculine pitch in men’s voices as short-term partners compared to long-term partners is positively associated with the extent that they attribute physical dominance to men with a low-pitched voice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
women's preferences for men with masculine voices is not a simple matter of "liking" masculine voices, but instead depends on the perceived personality of the man who speaks with a masculine voice.
the effect of relationship type on women's masculinity preference is mediated by perceived personality attributions.

variation in the effect of the relationship context on women’s preferences for men’s vocal pitch is predicted by individual differences in the perceived personality characteristics of men with low pitch.
The main takeaway from our work is that

individual differences in perceptions of physical characteristics and personality attributes can influence women's preferences for masculinity in men's voices, and thus, may be an important factor in shaping women's mate choices and, potentially, other types of social judgments.

women's perceptions of the personalities of men with low (masculine) voice pitch may be an important factor in explaining individual differences in the effects of relationship context on preferences for masculine pitch.

individual differences in perceptions of physical masculinity and antisocial personality characteristics may contribute to individual differences in the effects of relationship context on preferences for masculine men.
